articles.title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
articles.summary: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A.
body: Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.

It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
articles.summary: After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation.
body: In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation.

After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.

I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.

articles.title: Many languages, one common neural code
articles.summary: Analyzing speakers of 21 languages, an MIT study using multilingual AI finds the human brain may represent meaning in much the same way.
body: Languages take on thousands of forms. Some are tonal, like Vietnamese, where shifts in pitch convey distinct meanings. English relies on precise word orders, but this matters less for Russian, where words can be swapped without changing the intended message.
Despite so much variety in the linguistic kingdom, an MIT study has found that the human brain may process all sorts of languages in a universal way.

Artificial intelligence made this finding possible. In the study published today in Nature Neuroscience, the researchers used multilingual models to predict how the human brain responds to various languages. Those models also helped the researchers detect a shared brain process across people who collectively spoke 21 different languages.

“Of course, there are many differences in the ways humans converse with each other. But our team found that there is something fundamentally similar in how the brain communicates,” says Evelina Fedorenko, who is an investigator at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research, an associate professor of brain and cognitive sciences, and the senior author of the paper.

articles.title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
articles.summary: Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests.
body: Anthropic is bringing new AI tools to software engineers with Claude Ship.

Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude’s code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October. What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.

PR Steward “jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members” and leaves comments on what it changed, according to Anthropic. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes if an organization’s policy allows it. “Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language,” Anthropic says.
Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

articles.title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
articles.summary: The company’s board of directors has reinstated Huang a little more than a week after the CEO resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report.
body: Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.

The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.

In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is Nvidia’s Stock
articles.summary: Jensen Huang comes back, numbers go up. Maybe the reason behind the CEO’s return is just that simple?
body: The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars.

Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees. Each report chipped away at the company’s value until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the past month.

Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said during the company’s earnings call that the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” WIRED also reported that Nvidia’s board had been alarmed by Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying.”

And yet, despite all this, the board announced on Monday that it had brought Huang back— with some help from the US government. Semafor reported that, hours before Huang was reinstated, President Donald Trump dialed into the publicly traded company’s board meeting to argue for the ousted CEO’s return.
points: Maybe the reason behind the CEO’s return is just that simple?

articles.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
articles.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing.
body: Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

articles.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
articles.summary: Using agent teams and formal verification to improve quantum algorithms for fusion and chemistry.
body: Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support.

In a new paper, we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library, problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.

Because we cannot test resource-intensive quantum circuits on classical computers or today's small quantum processors, we have to prove that they work mathematically. Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover.
We chose to focus on applications that could one day impact some of humanity’s greatest challenges, such as clean energy and drug design, but our method is not limited to these problem areas.

articles.title: States Sue SpaceX Over Grok Deepfakes
articles.summary: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing several of Elon Musk’s companies, alleging they implemented weak safeguards against sexualized imagery of real people, including children.
body: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing Elon Musk ’s SpaceX, alleging that the company violated consumer protection laws by lying to users about both the safety of its generative AI tools and how seriously the company took stopping child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and nonconsensual intimate imagery from proliferating on its platforms. The suits follow a slew of other lawsuits against Musk’s companies around similar issues, including from the city of Baltimore and teens in Tennessee.

The attorneys general are each filing their own complaints in their respective state courts—Virginia in the circuit court for the city of Richmond, and Oregon in Multnomah County circuit court. Both suits name SpaceX and X Corp., the SpaceX subsidiary responsible for the social media platform X. SpaceX acquired xAI, the Musk startup and parent company of X Corp., in February. In doing so it also took ownership of Grok, which is at the center of the allegations in the suit.

articles.title: AI-driven technique could help engineers design analog chips faster and with less expense
articles.summary: The “SLIC” training method enables a small LLM to compete with much more resource-intensive models in complex circuit design tasks.
body: A new technique developed by MIT researchers could help engineers use artificial intelligence to streamline the design and innovation of analog integrated circuits, semiconductor chips that perform vital functions like communication and power management in electronic devices.

In the future, this method could allow engineers to prototype faster, explore a wider range of chip designs, and discover new design schemes that might improve the performance and energy efficiency of robots, medical monitors, or industrial sensors.

Designing analog integrated circuits that meet specific requirements is usually a cumbersome manual process due to the enormous number of possibilities. Frontier generative AI models have shown success in automating the process, but using these resource-intensive, cloud-hosted models could expose proprietary circuit design and semiconductor foundry data to malicious users.

The MIT method, called Small LM Iterating on Circuits, or SLIC (pronounced “slick”), enables engineers to train a small language model to perform analog circuit design as well as or better than a frontier large language model (LLM).

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
articles.summary: As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.
body: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
points: As AI-generated code piles up, Anthropic's new developer tools aim to eliminate another bottleneck by letting agents handle routine approvals.

articles.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
articles.summary: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.
body: AI investing startup Supertake has an interesting premise: What if your “takes” on the market could make you money without you having to pick stocks yourself? The service lets people turn their ideas into real investment portfolios, using frontier AI models and trading agents.

Now, the company has raised $20 million in seed funding to grow its business. The round was led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined, including Nat Friedman, who’s currently head of product at Meta Superintelligence Labs; Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch; renowned product manager Nikita Bier; investor Scott Belsky; and Nemil Dalal, a former Coinbase exec who is now a visiting partner at Y Combinator.
